union.text: the Minangkabau highlands (darek) and rantau, West Sumatra

land.text: Dharmasraya and the Minangkabau highlands: 'in 1347 Adityawarman proclaimed himself king in Malayapura'

predecessors.note: The Melayu page names Pagaruyung first among its successors.

land.text: the Minangkabau highlands, where the last sultan was arrested on 2 May 1833 and the Dutch took over

successors.note: Dutch rule in the highlands dates from the 1821 agreement and the Padri War; the Cliopatria row for the Dutch East Indies begins in 1800.

capitals.name: Pagaruyung (near Batusangkar)
capitals.note: 'a kingdom in the Minangkabau highlands at Pagaruyung'. The palace on Batu Patah Hill burned in 1804 in the Padri War, the Padri occupied Pagaruyung in 1815 and the sultan fled; the Dutch pushed the Padri out on 4 March 1822. The infobox gives no capital.

correction.text: the Minangkabau highlands (darek) and rantau, West Sumatra

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The highlands (Luhak Tanah Datar, Agam and Limapuluh Koto) and the rantau to the coast are drawn as West Sumatra, the gazetteer's Minangkabau region (about 42,000 km2); the pages give no area and no frontier. 'presided over the central Sumatra region between 1347 and 1375'; the Rantau (Kampar, Siak, Jambi, Indragiri, Pasaman, Barus, Pariaman) carry no dates on the page and are not drawn. Infobox area: none.

the west coast of West Sumatra (Padang, Pariaman) under Aceh's governors

correction.text: the Minangkabau highlands and the rantau inland, without the west coast that Aceh's governors held from the early 17th century and the VOC from 1666

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In the early 17th century, the kingdom was forced to recognise the sovereignty of the Sultanate of Aceh'; Aceh-appointed governors held the west coast until the Minang there rebelled (about 1665) and the VOC expelled Aceh in 1666; the sultanate dossier (sultanate-of-aceh) hands the coast to the VOC that year, so it is not returned here. The Padri occupation of Pagaruyung (1815-1822) is an occupation event, not a change of shape.

region.text: the Minangkabau highlands (darek) and rantau, West Sumatra

ledger.note: 1347: Adityawarman proclaims himself king in Malayapura. 'in 1347 Adityawarman proclaimed himself king in Malayapura' and 'presided over the central Sumatra region between 1347 and 1375'; the Minangkabau page: he 'founded a kingdom in the Minangkabau highlands at Pagaruyung and ruled between 1347 and 1375'. The Melayu page: he conquered Tanah Datar 'to control the gold trade'.

region.text: the west coast of West Sumatra (Padang, Pariaman) under Aceh's governors

ledger.note: c. 1609: Aceh's governors take the west coast. 'In the early 17th century, the kingdom was forced to recognise the sovereignty of the Sultanate of Aceh'; the page gives no year, 1609 is the step the sultanate-of-aceh dossier uses (it carries the matching gain and a vassal span of Pagaruyung to 1666).

region.text: the west coast of West Sumatra (Padang, Pariaman) under Aceh's governors

ledger.note: c. 1665: the Minang of the west coast rise against Aceh. 'around 1665, the Minang people on the west coast rose up and rebelled against the Aceh governors'; the VOC had first arrived in 1663.

region.text: the west coast of West Sumatra (Padang, Pariaman) under Aceh's governors

ledger.note: 1666: Aceh is expelled from the west coast. 'expelling the Sultanate of Aceh from the coast of West Sumatra in 1666'; the VOC wrote on 9 October 1668 that it had taken control of the coast, so the coast does not return to Pagaruyung's shape (the sultanate-of-aceh dossier hands it to the VOC).

region.text: the Minangkabau highlands (darek) and rantau, West Sumatra

ledger.note: 1803: the Padri civil war begins in the highlands. The Padri War 'was fought from 1803 until 1837 in West Sumatra' (Minangkabau page: 'A civil war started in 1803 with the Padri fundamentalist Islamic group'); the Padri need their own rebel dossier (padri-movement).

1815: the Padri occupy Pagaruyung. 'The Padri under Tuanku Pasaman occupied the Pagaruyung Kingdom in 1815' and the sultan fled the capital; the Pagaruyung page: 'most of the Minangkabau royal family were killed in 1815'.

4 March 1822: the Dutch drive the Padri out of Pagaruyung. 'On 4 March 1822, Dutch troops succeeded in pushing the Padri people out of Pagaruyung'; the Minangkabau nobility had made its deal with the Dutch in Padang in February 1821 (the Padri War page says 21 February, the Pagaruyung page 10 February), 'a sign of the submission of the kingdom of Pagaruyung to the Dutch government'.

region.text: the Minangkabau highlands (darek) and rantau, West Sumatra

ledger.note: 1833: the sultan's arrest ends the kingdom's part in the Padri War. The war itself runs on under the Dutch until 'on 16 August 1837, Fort Bonjol was completely conquered'.

region.text: the Minangkabau highlands under the arrested sultan

ledger.note: 2 May 1833: the Dutch take the highlands. 'On 2 May 1833 Sultan Tunggul Alam Bagagar was arrested by Lieutenant Colonel Cornelis Pieter Jacob Elout' at Batusangkar and banished to Batavia.

region.text: the kingdom's territory in the Minangkabau highlands

ledger.note: 1833: the Pagaruyung Kingdom ends with the sultan's arrest. The page's span is 1347-1833; it also says Sultan Arifin Muningsyah, 'the last king in Minangkabau', died in 1825 and that the 1821 agreement had already submitted the kingdom to the Dutch.

wars.name: Padri War

zones.text: Tanah Datar, Agam, Lima Puluh Kota, Bonjol and Rao, the places the page names

wars.outcome: The Padri occupied Pagaruyung in 1815; the Minangkabau nobility allied with the Dutch in 1821, the Dutch pushed the Padri out of Pagaruyung on 4 March 1822, the sultan was arrested on 2 May 1833, and 'on 16 August 1837, Fort Bonjol was completely conquered'.
wars.note: The Pagaruyung page writes the war as 1803-1838 only in a citation title; the Padri War page's text gives 1837. The kingdom's own part ends in 1833.

wars.name: Minang rising against Aceh and the VOC expulsion of Aceh

zones.text: the west coast of West Sumatra (Padang, Pariaman) under Aceh's governors

wars.outcome: 'expelling the Sultanate of Aceh from the coast of West Sumatra in 1666'; the VOC letter of 9 October 1668 reports it had taken the coast.
wars.note: The Aceh dossier hands the coast to the VOC (dutch-republic) in 1666.

wars.name: Majapahit expedition against Pagaruyung (possible)
wars.outcome: 'Majapahit possibly sent another expedition to conquer the kingdom in 1409'; no result stated.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer sees it was considered; the page is uncertain ('possibly').

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the highlands are a mountain core with undated rantau. The 1821 agreement is a submission, not a boundary.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for Pagaruyung or the Minangkabau. Wikidata id not looked up (wikidata.org unreachable): null. Every shape is the gazetteer's Minangkabau region (West Sumatra), because the pages give no frontier and date none of the rantau (Kampar, Siak, Jambi, Indragiri, Pasaman, Barus, Pariaman); the Adityawarman page says he used the Majapahit office of wreddamantri 'to pursue military expansion and take the east coast of Sumatra' without date or name, so no eastern land is drawn and a gap-filler should open a page on Kampar, Siak or Indragiri. The Pagaruyung page says the kingdom 'was finally transformed into an Islamic sultanate' in the 17th century without a year; no rename event was written. The sultanate-of-aceh dossier carries the matching gain (c. 1609) and a vassal span of Pagaruyung to 1666. The Padri need a dossier of type rebel (padri-movement, 1803-1837); the dutch-east-indies dossier should carry the 1821 submission as a vassal span and the 1833 gain. The rulers list is omitted: the pages give only Adityawarman (1347-1375), his son Ananggawarman, and the last kings (Arifin Muningsyah d. 1825, Tunggul Alam Bagagarsyah arrested 1833). Gazetteer: Batusangkar and Pariaman are not in places.jsonl (coordinates used).
